subTitleDesc.sub_title_en:
1 Understanding legal methodologies.
2 Understanding legal methodologies that can be applied in problem-solving and legal research.
3 Applying legal methodologies in problem-solving and legal research.
4 Understanding legal methodologies employed in legal research in different legal traditions.
5 Applying legal methodologies employed in legal research in different legal traditions.
subTitleDesc.sub_describe_en: This class intends to introduce legal methodologies employed in legal research. It starts from the introduction and criticism of Utilitarianism prevalent in Western world, in order to enable students to compare it with the Analytical Legal Positivism traditionally adopted by most Taiwanese legal research. To meet the requirement of flipped classroom and EMI, this class takes advantage of Michael J. Sandel’s Harvard Open Class - Justice: What's the Right Thing to Do? – as the medium to learn professional English in our designed teaching method.

description.describe_ch: 本課程著重法學方法中各派學說之引介，由西方最具代表性之功利主義思考的批判出發，讓同學能省思在傳統大陸法學著重之分析實證主義法學之外，西方盛行之功利主義法學論述之利弊。本課程採用翻轉教學之設計，課程採用哈佛大學教授桑戴爾（Michael J. Sandel）講授正義的線上課程，由該課程出發，進一步引介其他法學方法理論，以期能同時滿足EMI課程之要求，讓同學能漸進式地提升英文學習能力。

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol: 請益時間的說明 您可以在我約定的每週請益時間裡，我可以直接回答您的問題及討論課程內容，利用iLearn中Teams頻道、或親自到我的請益時間。如果您在課程學習上需要幫助，但因日程安排有衝突而無法出席我約定的請益時間，請先給我發送電子郵件，另外在安排預約時間。與學生交談是我工作的一大亮點 - 我期待與您交談！
gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
Classrooms Protocol
Diversity and Inclusion
All course activities will be carried out in an atmosphere of friendly participation and interaction among students, respecting and appreciating each student's personal experience, background and perspectives, such as various school systems at home and abroad, diverse enrollment and learning cultures, gender, etc. You are expected to apply the highest academic standards throughout this course and to treat fellow students with dignity and respect.
Expected classroom behavior
Behavior in the classroom should always be prompt, professional, prepared, and courteous. Effective learning can only be achieved by maintaining mutual dignity and mutual respect among classmates, teachers or other lecturers. In order to ensure a conducive learning environment, everyone is expected to do the following, abide by each other's classroom behavior rules, and get used to a culture of politeness.
Students should attend class on time. If you cannot arrive at the class on time due to your class time, please do not register for the class. Unless you are sick or there is an emergency, you should be in your classroom on time and in your seat before class starts. If you have to leave class early for any reason, please let me know in advance.
All students are expected to treat everyone with respect in the classroom and to behave reasonably, responsibly, and courteously at all times.
Do not talk, read, sleep or do other non-course-related homework during class, except for group discussions, otherwise marginal conversations should be minimized. If you are sitting next to someone who might be chatting with you during class, move to another seat so you don't give in to temptation.
You should listen attentively when classmates present or ask questions. When you present, you should speak loudly to your group or class so that they can hear you clearly.
Laptops or tablets are allowed to take notes in class, otherwise they should be put away.
Make sure that mobile devices such as mobile phones and PDAs are turned off during class, and put away and keep silent.
Students are not allowed to wear earphones in class.
Dress neatly without revealing.
It is hoped that the content of the course rules will be described in a professional dialogue mode of the highest standard and mutual respect, with diversity and inclusiveness.
Teachers are able to guide students in ways, what students should do in the learning process, and their due responsibilities.
Course Communication and Netiquette Guidelines
All students shall abide by the following communication regulations:
Teaching and learning uses o365 mailbox as a common tool for teachers and students to communicate in teaching and learning.
When communicating with teachers and classmates in emails, bulletin boards, etc., write the information clearly and be polite.
Your e-mail must be signed, I will not reply to "anonymous" letters.
I have to check the spelling, grammar and punctuation of the letter. I will not reply to you whether the email is good or not.
From Monday to Friday, if anyone asks questions about course learning, I will reply to the email within 24 hours. If you just send me information (eg "I will be absent this Friday."), I will not write back to you.
The online classroom is still a classroom. Although classes are taught mostly online, appropriate classroom behavior must still be observed. Respecting fellow students and teachers is just as important online as it is in the classroom. This course arranges multiple learning tasks to be carried out online in iLearn. You should set aside time to actively participate in online activities and complete all delivered learning tasks. In iLearn, you can interact with your classmates through various online activities and course content to complete course activities.
In each online discussion area, do not dominate any discussion strongly, but give other students the opportunity to participate in the discussion, so as to improve the learning experience of everyone in the course.
Everyone should keep an open mind and respect minority opinions, even you can express different opinions.
Present your ideas appropriately and avoid vulgar or offensive language. Language is easily misunderstood in written communication. If you must emphasize a point, review the statement to make sure no one is offended; then make a statement. Humor and sarcasm can easily be misunderstood, so try to be factual and professional.
Write according to the theme, focus and express briefly, and keep it. Online courses require a lot of reading. When writing, keep your sentences to the point and short so that readers don't get lost in lengthy paragraphs and miss the point of your statement.
Read first, then write. Please be sure to read all postings or comments before posting a comment to prevent duplicating comments or asking questions that have already been answered.
Write a comment text, which should be reviewed and re-reviewed before sending. Sent comments cannot be retracted, so it is important to double check all text to ensure that the intended message is clearly conveyed.
The language of network communication. Do not write in all caps and avoid excessive use of emoji, although the use of emoji can help convey non-verbal feeling, excessive use can cause reading difficulties, misinterpretation, such as: (#－.－), o(≧ v≦)o, (￣﹏￣), (￣︶￣)>, ￣⊙￣⊙︽.
Avoid using local language or slang, which may lead to misunderstanding.
Share tips with other students and don't make fun of someone's reading and dictation skills.
Consider the privacy of others. Ask permission before giving out email addresses or other information about classmates.
Do not publish inappropriate information. Do not forward virus warnings, chain letters, jokes, etc. to classmates or teachers. Sharing pornographic or insensitive content is prohibited.
Student Responsibilities Student Responsibilities
Before the start of each semester registration, go to the MyFCU personal information form to confirm the basic information you have left in Feng Chia University. Including mobile phone number, email address, correspondence address and other contact information, so that teachers, teaching assistants, or staff of the course offering unit can contact you.
Confirm that your Feng Chia University o365 email and NID password are activated. This will be required for identity verification and use of electronic resources, such as online classrooms, library resources, software resources, access control, online courses, personal learning history, MyFCU App and other resources.
You should read and understand the syllabus requirements of this course in detail, update the latest information in real time, and manage your study time well.
Check your Feng Chia University email and log in to iLearn at any time to understand the information released by this course.
Abide by integrity, should maintain a high degree of professionalism, actively attend and participate in the learning commitment of this classroom, and behave with integrity in and out of the classroom.
Use library collections and copyrighted textbooks.
You should fill in the mid-term and final course teaching feedback for this course according to the week and session listed in the teaching progress and content. Your participation and feedback will help me improve my teaching skills, course teaching content and arrangement of activities, and also provide crucial opinions
gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno:
https://ethics.moe.edu.tw/files/resource/ebook/file/ebook_02_cn.pdf
"給大學生的參考手冊─ 在高等教育課堂中實踐學術誠信 前 言 相信多數的老師與學生都認同學術誠信（academic integrity，亦稱學術倫理）的重要性， 並理解學術誠信是在教學過程中不可或缺的重要元素。然而，身為學生的你，當被授課老師與指 導老師們再三叮嚀要遵守學術誠信時，是否曾覺得虛無飄渺或無所適從？因為你不太確定，究竟 什麼是學術誠信？ 在新生始業輔導的教育課程，或新修某一門課的第一週，老師們可能會秀出學校的校規或學 則，用當中的違反學術倫理態樣去提醒你不該做的事（如不可抄襲與造假）。此時或許你會疑惑： 只要不做違規的事，就代表我是個有學術誠信的學生嗎？若是如此，那不違規又是指什麼呢？是 不要違反列出的這些項目就好嗎？那做了但沒被老師抓到，就可以不算違規嗎？如果情節輕微可 以通融嗎？又或是不僅不能做違規事，也要心存正念，達到表裡合一的境界，才算有學術誠信？ 誠信與否的那條紅線到底落在哪裡？ 事實上，學術誠信是個正向的名詞，其內涵是由諸多正面的價值組成，需要大學校園師生由 行動來共同守護。如果只是用不能做的違規行為去詮釋學術誠信，不但在解釋上相當片面，也不 可能涵蓋到所有的學習情境。此時，若同學換到一個新的環境（如到國外讀研究所），或需要面 對更複雜的學習任務時（如參加校外的國際競賽、爭取獎學金等），也有機會面臨在可為與不可 為之間的矛盾與掙扎。因此，縱使認識違規行為的態樣很重要，但我們也應該由內而外地澈底理 解學術誠信，包含其所蘊含的價值觀與實踐方式。唯有如此，無論日後面對什麼樣的學習情境， 我們只要秉持這些價值原則行事，即能達到學術界對於學生在課業活動上所規範的倫理標準，當 然也不會讓自己陷入違反學術誠信的風險。"---以下請自行連結參閱
gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno_en:
You are expected to:
1 act in a way that is honest, fair, respectful and responsible in your studies and academic work;  
2 uphold the highest standards of academic integrity;
3 be fair and honest in all interactions with members of this class;
4 abstain from cheating, lying, and stealing.
 
Learning must be based on honesty. Any student who attempts to use a work that he has not produced as his own is considered dishonest. Students who cheat or plagiarize in homework, tests or exams, or assist others, will be scored as zero. If they are repeat offenders, they will be submitted in accordance with the rewards and punishments for students of Feng Chia University.
  • It is considered cheating if you copy someone else's answers during an assessment, or if you turn in a paper or assignment that was written in whole or in part by someone else when you turned in an assignment.
  • It is considered cheating if you copy someone else's answers during an assessment, or if you turn in a paper or assignment that was written in whole or in part by someone else when you turned in an assignment.

When communicating with teachers and classmates in emails, bulletin boards, etc., write the information clearly and be polite.
Your e-mail must be signed, I will not reply to "anonymous" letters.
I have to check the spelling, grammar and punctuation of the letter. I will not reply to you whether the email is good or not.
From Monday to Friday, if anyone asks questions about course learning, I will reply to the email within 24 hours. If you just send me information (eg "I will be absent this Friday."), I will not write back to you.
The online classroom is still a classroom. Although classes are taught mostly online, appropriate classroom behavior must still be observed. Respecting fellow students and teachers is just as important online as it is in the classroom. This course arranges multiple learning tasks to be carried out online in iLearn. You should set aside time to actively participate in online activities and complete all delivered learning tasks. In iLearn, you can interact with your classmates through various online activities and course content to complete course activities.
In each online discussion area, do not dominate any discussion strongly, but give other students the opportunity to participate in the discussion, so as to improve the learning experience of everyone in the course.
Everyone should keep an open mind and respect minority opinions, even you can express different opinions.
Present your ideas appropriately and avoid vulgar or offensive language. Language is easily misunderstood in written communication. If you must emphasize a point, review the statement to make sure no one is offended; then make a statement. Humor and sarcasm can easily be misunderstood, so try to be factual and professional.
Write according to the theme, focus and express briefly, and keep it. Online courses require a lot of reading. When writing, keep your sentences to the point and short so that readers don't get lost in lengthy paragraphs and miss the point of your statement.
Read first, then write. Please be sure to read all postings or comments before posting a comment to prevent duplicating comments or asking questions that have already been answered.
Write a comment text, which should be reviewed and re-reviewed before sending. Sent comments cannot be retracted, so it is important to double check all text to ensure that the intended message is clearly conveyed.
The language of network communication. Do not write in all caps and avoid excessive use of emoji, although the use of emoji can help convey non-verbal feeling, excessive use can cause reading difficulties, misinterpretation, such as: (#－.－), o(≧ v≦)o, (￣﹏￣), (￣︶￣)>, ￣⊙￣⊙︽.
Avoid using local language or slang, which may lead to misunderstanding.
Share tips with other students and don't make fun of someone's reading and dictation skills.
Consider the privacy of others. Ask permission before giving out email addresses or other information about classmates.
Do not publish inappropriate information. Do not forward virus warnings, chain letters, jokes, etc. to classmates or teachers. Sharing pornographic or insensitive content is prohibited.
Student Responsibilities Student Responsibilities
Before the start of each semester registration, go to the MyFCU personal information form to confirm the basic information you have left in Feng Chia University. Including mobile phone number, email address, correspondence address and other contact information, so that teachers, teaching assistants, or staff of the course offering unit can contact you.
Confirm that your Feng Chia University o365 email and NID password are activated. This will be required for identity verification and use of electronic resources, such as online classrooms, library resources, software resources, access control, online courses, personal learning history, MyFCU App and other resources.
You should read and understand the syllabus requirements of this course in detail, update the latest information in real time, and manage your study time well.
Check your Feng Chia University email and log in to iLearn at any time to understand the information released by this course.
Abide by integrity, should maintain a high degree of professionalism, actively attend and participate in the learning commitment of this classroom, and behave with integrity in and out of the classroom.
Use library collections and copyrighted textbooks.
You should fill in the mid-term and final course teaching feedback for this course according to the week and session listed in the teaching progress and content. Your participation and feedback will help me improve my teaching skills, course teaching content and arrangement of activities, and also provide crucial opinions

https://ethics.moe.edu.tw/files/resource/ebook/file/ebook_02_cn.pdf
"給大學生的參考手冊─ 在高等教育課堂中實踐學術誠信 前 言 相信多數的老師與學生都認同學術誠信（academic integrity，亦稱學術倫理）的重要性， 並理解學術誠信是在教學過程中不可或缺的重要元素。然而，身為學生的你，當被授課老師與指 導老師們再三叮嚀要遵守學術誠信時，是否曾覺得虛無飄渺或無所適從？因為你不太確定，究竟 什麼是學術誠信？ 在新生始業輔導的教育課程，或新修某一門課的第一週，老師們可能會秀出學校的校規或學 則，用當中的違反學術倫理態樣去提醒你不該做的事（如不可抄襲與造假）。此時或許你會疑惑： 只要不做違規的事，就代表我是個有學術誠信的學生嗎？若是如此，那不違規又是指什麼呢？是 不要違反列出的這些項目就好嗎？那做了但沒被老師抓到，就可以不算違規嗎？如果情節輕微可 以通融嗎？又或是不僅不能做違規事，也要心存正念，達到表裡合一的境界，才算有學術誠信？ 誠信與否的那條紅線到底落在哪裡？ 事實上，學術誠信是個正向的名詞，其內涵是由諸多正面的價值組成，需要大學校園師生由 行動來共同守護。如果只是用不能做的違規行為去詮釋學術誠信，不但在解釋上相當片面，也不 可能涵蓋到所有的學習情境。此時，若同學換到一個新的環境（如到國外讀研究所），或需要面 對更複雜的學習任務時（如參加校外的國際競賽、爭取獎學金等），也有機會面臨在可為與不可 為之間的矛盾與掙扎。因此，縱使認識違規行為的態樣很重要，但我們也應該由內而外地澈底理 解學術誠信，包含其所蘊含的價值觀與實踐方式。唯有如此，無論日後面對什麼樣的學習情境， 我們只要秉持這些價值原則行事，即能達到學術界對於學生在課業活動上所規範的倫理標準，當 然也不會讓自己陷入違反學術誠信的風險。"---以下請自行連結參閱
policy.ais_meno_en:
You are expected to:
1 act in a way that is honest, fair, respectful and responsible in your studies and academic work;  
2 uphold the highest standards of academic integrity;
3 be fair and honest in all interactions with members of this class;
4 abstain from cheating, lying, and stealing.
 
Learning must be based on honesty. Any student who attempts to use a work that he has not produced as his own is considered dishonest. Students who cheat or plagiarize in homework, tests or exams, or assist others, will be scored as zero. If they are repeat offenders, they will be submitted in accordance with the rewards and punishments for students of Feng Chia University.
  • It is considered cheating if you copy someone else's answers during an assessment, or if you turn in a paper or assignment that was written in whole or in part by someone else when you turned in an assignment.
